newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian car market finally looking up - CSP.
newsitem.headline: Italian car market finally looking up - CSP.

text.p: The Italian car market is starting to shown signs of a recovery after four years of stagnation, leading auto sector research group Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) said.
CSP welcomed data published on Friday which showed new car registrations jumped 12.14 percent in December year-on-year and posted a modest 0.34 percent increase for 1996 as a whole.

It said in a statement that already in December, before the government announced a car incentive scheme, dealers polled said order books had begun to show an improvement with sales over the last 1996 quarter rising by 5.8 percent.

In its January survey, now details of the scheme for bonuses for motorists swapping old cars for new have been revealed, the percentage of dealers expecting to see increased sales has risen from 16 percent in November to 55 percent.
Those still pessimistic now only account for seven percent against 22 percent in November.
In the period of the scheme's planned implementation to the end of September, the incentives are expected to result in extra sales of some 200,000 new cars, CSP said.
It forecast total 1997 sales at around 2.0 million against 1996's 1.74 million.

"The bonus scheme for scrapping cars over 10 years old in exchange for buying a new car has come at a very good time," said CSP director Gianprimo Quaglino. CSP has been one of the leading voices calling for an incentive scheme to boost depressed domestic sales.

"The measures are coming in at a time when the market is showing a slight recovery, even though volume is still small, and may form a bridge between the long period of stagnation and a real recovery which the market could build on under its own steam," he added.
Italian carmakers association agreed that the introduction of the incentives scheme which "have sparked a hope of seeing a return of demand" to the market.
For 1997, including the effects of the scheme, Anfia forecast demand at between 1.95 and 2.0 million vehicles.
